stem: Environmental-services staff are performing terminal cleaning of a room managed under Contact Precautions. Which PPE is appropriate for the cleaning task?

options.A: Gloves alone because clothing protection is unnecessary once the client has left the room.
options.B: A surgical mask and eye protection without gloves because Contact Precautions end when the client leaves.
options.C: A gown or protective apron plus appropriate reusable cleaning gloves.
options.D: An N95 respirator without gown or gloves because airborne protection replaces contact-barrier PPE during terminal cleaning.

rationale: CDC environmental-cleaning guidance lists gown and/or plastic apron plus reusable rubber gloves for routine and terminal cleaning of areas under Contact Precautions. Required transmission-based PPE remains relevant during terminal cleaning because cleaning staff can contact contaminated environmental surfaces and equipment. Therefore C is correct. A omits indicated clothing protection, B omits gloves and uses PPE not sufficient for Contact Precautions, and D substitutes airborne respiratory protection for the gown/glove barrier required for this task.
educational_objective: Use gown/apron and reusable cleaning gloves during terminal environmental cleaning of areas under Contact Precautions, following transmission-based PPE requirements for the cleaning task.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Cleaning Supplies and Equipment — Best Practices for Environmental Cleaning in Global Healthcare Facilities with Limited Resources
source_version_date: CDC page March 19, 2024; live currentness rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Section 3.4 Personal protective equipment for environmental cleaning > Table 5: Contact precautions (routine and terminal cleaning) require gown and/or plastic apron plus reusable rubber gloves. Best practices state required PPE should be donned before entering and removed before leaving the patient-care area as appropriate.
source_claim_supported: Terminal cleaning in a Contact Precautions environment requires gown/apron and reusable cleaning gloves; respiratory protection alone does not replace contact-barrier PPE.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: select appropriate PPE, maintain transmission-based precautions, and prevent environmental transmission during cleaning/disinfection.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE for terminal cleaning under Contact Precautions

source_original.stem: Environmental-services staff are performing terminal cleaning of a room that was managed under Contact Precautions. Which PPE is appropriate for the cleaning task?

options.A: Wear gloves alone because clothing protection is unnecessary once the client has left the room.
options.B: Wear a surgical mask and eye protection without gloves because Contact Precautions apply only while the client is present.
options.C: Wear a gown or protective apron and gloves appropriate for terminal cleaning in a Contact Precautions environment.
options.D: Wear an N95 respirator without gown or gloves because airborne protection replaces contact-barrier PPE during terminal cleaning.

source_original.rationale: CDC environmental-cleaning guidance lists gown/apron and reusable gloves for routine and terminal cleaning of areas under Contact Precautions. The original vague statement was narrowed to the PPE recommended for this specific cleaning task.
source_original.source_detail: PPE table: Contact Precautions routine and terminal cleaning require gown/apron and gloves Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the environmental-cleaning PPE construct and key C, aligned the PPE wording directly with CDC Table 5, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct task-specific PPE recommendation.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC environmental-cleaning guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC Cleaning Supplies and Equipment page live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC section 3.4 > Table 5 Contact Precautions routine/terminal cleaning
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the exact CDC PPE combination for Contact Precautions cleaning and does not infer additional mask/eye protection unless another task-specific splash risk exists.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because CDC includes gown/apron in addition to gloves for Contact Precautions cleaning.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because gloves are required and surgical mask/eye protection alone does not meet Contact Precautions cleaning PPE.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because an N95 is associated with airborne precautions and does not replace gown/gloves for contact contamination.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C matches the CDC Table 5 PPE combination for routine/terminal Contact Precautions cleaning.
audit_findings.cueing: All options specify PPE combinations for the same task and environment.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based PPE and environmental cleaning safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current CDC Table 5 and environmental-cleaning procedures, all four alternatives, rationale, objective, ambiguity, cueing, and NCSBN category alignment. C remained uniquely correct.
